book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Items of furniture left, for example, in front of the stage

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming in front of something means being placed before it, so the first piece leads

parts.note: the left is one example of a side
'the boards' is a theatre term for the stage

explanation.surface: A stage manager arranges furniture in a set, putting some pieces to the left at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like stage left, part of the furniture's placing, but with 'for example' it just stands for any side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideboards are long cabinets for a dining room, so they count among household furniture.

clue.text: Party like this shall be heard!

indicators.note: being heard means spoken out loud, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: like this is so, said together with shall

explanation.surface: A host proclaims that a party in this style will take place.
explanation.walkthrough: Run together quickly, 'so shall' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering, as held by a club or church.

clue.text: Working mothers are first to get fruit

indicators.note: being first means placed at the front, so the mothers word leads the answer

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Employed mums are the first to buy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working mothers' reads as a single phrase, but the words split and the second goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark plum, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Dance directions that eliminate friction?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'things that eliminate friction', a plural noun

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
bearings are compass directions

explanation.surface: Steps called at a dance that keep the dancers moving smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the playful reading: a dance and some compass headings together describe a machine part.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are small steel balls between moving parts that reduce friction in machinery.

clue.text: Horse has a ban lifted

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A racehorse is allowed to run again after its suspension ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the ban word is turned up; the A stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula, prized for speed and stamina.

clue.text: Way of talking on a railway reference book

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: diction is manner of speaking
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A book about how people speak on the trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary lists words with their meanings, a standard reference work.

clue.text: The sort of chamber welcomed by a male chorus

indicators.note: something welcomed by a group is taken in among them, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A men's choir sings in a resonant hall that suits their voices.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'male' and 'chorus': the last letter of one and the first three of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo chamber is a room built to reverberate sound, so the answer names that kind of chamber.

clue.text: Number one in the church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a counting number such as one, two, three
second meaning: a senior Roman Catholic prelate

explanation.surface: The top figure in a church hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a single phrase meaning the leader; it splits into 'Number' and 'one in the church'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the ordinary counting numbers, and a cardinal is a high-ranking member of the Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Shaping a tree top is a bit of a performance!

indicators.note: shaping something works it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Topiary on the crown of a tree is quite a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a performance' is an idiom for a fuss, but here means a short operatic work.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera, so it is literally a little piece of musical theatre.

clue.text: Policeman is worried by initially cautious cooperation

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and disturbed, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the opening letter of cautious

explanation.surface: An anxious officer is unsettled by a suspect who is careful in helping with enquiries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' wants to be a short synonym such as PC or DI; here all nine letters are used whole and shuffled with one extra C.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliance is going along with what is asked, which is a form of cooperation.

clue.text: Couple caught out by bank

indicators.note: out means removed or excluded, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Two cricketers are dismissed, caught by a fielder on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACE loses its C to leave BRAE. A brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or steep bank.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a brae is a slope or hillside, especially a river bank, so it is a kind of bank.

clue.text: What flypaper does to other creatures

definitions.text: What flypaper does to other creatures

parts.words: What flypaper does to other creatures
parts.note: surface reading: a sticky strip trapping bugs besides flies
setter's reading: the phrase describes what flypaper does to the bugs, and also names a type of insect that looks like a twig

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb phrase, it says flypaper glues bugs; read as a noun, it is the name of twig-like insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Stick insects are long thin insects resembling twigs, and flypaper literally sticks insects.

clue.text: A degree covering minute old English life-form

indicators.note: a thing covering another wraps round it, so the degree goes outside what follows

parts.note: taken as written
a Bachelor of Arts degree
M is the abbreviation for minute
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: An arts degree course spends a tiny amount of time on an ancient English creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective, tiny, which suits a microscopic organism; it is the time unit's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a simple microscopic form of life.

clue.text: Rant from family after needing help to get back

indicators.note: after says the family word follows the other piece in the answer
getting back means going the opposite way, so the word for help is read from right to left

parts.note: aid is help
a tribe is a family group or clan

explanation.surface: Someone in need of assistance to return home gets an angry outburst from relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family' sits before the help word in the clue, but 'after' moves it to the end; 'needing' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a long angry speech, which is what a rant is.

clue.text: Mad appeals somehow bring a lump to the throat

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unspecified new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Wild, desperate pleas move listeners to the edge of tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring a lump to the throat' is an idiom for being moving; here the lump is a literal one on the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the projection of the larynx cartilage at the front of the neck.

clue.text: What's an airline pilot doing with skill — in a boat!

parts.note: a pilot bringing a plane down is landing it
craft means skill, as in a craftsman's

explanation.surface: A joke that an airline pilot is showing off his flying expertise in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a pilot oddly afloat; the answer is a military vessel for putting troops ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing craft is a flat-bottomed vessel used to carry troops or vehicles onto a beach, so it is a boat.

clue.text: The odds on impostor's dog

parts.note: SP is the starting price, a horse's odds when a race begins
a ringer is an impostor, as a substituted racehorse; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a fraudster's greyhound.
explanation.walkthrough: A ringer is racing slang for a disguised horse or dog run in another's place, which suits the betting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a springer spaniel, a breed of gundog.

clue.text: A couple of lags left by plane!

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for 'something left by a plane'

parts.note: first sense: a lag is a convict, and a con is another word for one
second sense: to lag is to fall behind, to trail

explanation.surface: Two convicts escaped by flying away.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word lags is used twice: a lag is a convict, and to lag is to trail behind. The exclamation mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrail is the white vapour trail that an aircraft leaves across the sky.

clue.text: Poor timing for rap affects the bottom line

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters that follow are in a faulty order to be fixed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rapper's bad timing hurts a record company's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bottom line' is the accountant's phrase for the final figure in a set of accounts, the profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line of accounts is the net figure showing what was earned, which a profit margin measures.

clue.text: Scrutinise each function

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'
a thing's use is its function

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine every role in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine something carefully, so it is to scrutinise.

clue.text: Nations, say, West of Sudan

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: the west of a word is its left-hand end, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the leftmost letter of Sudan

explanation.surface: Countries, for instance those lying to the west of Sudan in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', introducing nations; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: States are sovereign political countries, the same thing as nations.

clue.text: Whole grain? Let's be different

indicators.note: to be different is to be changed in form, so the letters before it take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks about wholegrain food and suggests trying something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whole grain' reads as one phrase, the health-food term; the first word is the definition and the second starts the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean entire or complete in itself, a formal synonym of whole.

clue.text: Permission given when broadcast

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a signal broadcast is sent out

explanation.surface: Approval granted when a programme is put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' tempts the solver to look for a sound-alike, but here it is simply a past participle meaning transmitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement or consent, permission that has been granted.

clue.text: In Scotland little money makes you cry

parts.note: wee is the Scots word for small
p is a penny, the smallest unit of British money

explanation.surface: Being poor north of the border leaves you in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, which is what crying means.

clue.text: It might bite back!

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the word for bite is read from its end

parts.note: tang is a sharp bite of flavour

explanation.surface: A warning about some creature that will retaliate if provoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a biting insect, while 'bite' turned round spells its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small fly, and many gnats bite people, so it is something that might bite.

clue.text: The aristocracy don't start dinner with leftover bread

indicators.note: not starting means missing the beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
the crust is the bit of bread often left uneaten

explanation.surface: Posh people refuse to begin a meal that comes with stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER loses its first letter to give UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper crust is an informal idiom for the highest social class, the aristocracy.

clue.text: The Italian is trapped between both sides in the stream

indicators.note: something trapped between two things sits inside them, with one on each side

parts.note: the two sides are right and left
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian man is stuck between two banks in the middle of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: IL goes between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small brook, so it is a kind of stream.

clue.text: Employees who would write to drug suppliers?

parts.note: to pen is to write
pushers are drug dealers

explanation.surface: Staff who would send letters to dealers in narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a pen-pusher, a clerk, is read as a dealer who writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pushers is a mildly scornful term for office workers doing routine paperwork, so they are employees.
